title: Install an old-work electrical box with its cable fed in: push it into the drywall cut-out, drive both clamp screws
instruction: The cable is already in the blue electrical box. Install the box in the hole in the wall: push it in until its ears are flat on the wall, with the cable going back into the wall behind it, then drive both of its clamp screws with the screwdriver until the box is held tight. Put the screwdriver down and take both hands away.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00, 821,000 US jobs in 2025) have the Core task "Fasten small metal or plastic boxes to walls to house electrical switches or outlets." In a finished wall that is an old-work box clamped to the drywall, as for nearly every switch or outlet added to an existing building. The method: "Once the fit is right, remove the box, run wires into it, and position the box back in the hole. Then use a screwdriver to tighten the screws that engage the box's tabs and lock it in place." The cable is stiff: it has to be pushed back into the wall ahead of the box without being drawn out of it, and it springs the box back out a few millimetres when the box is let go, so the box is not flat on the wall until a clamp draws it there. The box goes square into a cut-out 1.6 mm wider than it each side; each clamp screw is driven horizontally with a #2 Phillips tip in wrist strokes; the clamps are hidden behind the board, so the only sign one has gripped is the screw stalling.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. 1) Wall section (fixed; its bottom plate clamped to the table): 1/2 in (12.7 mm) gypsum drywall, 480 wide and 400 tall, its face at x 340 facing the arms, centred on y 0, fixed to a 2x4 (38 x 89 mm) pine bottom plate and top plate and two 2x4 studs 16 in (406 mm) on centre at y +-203; the back of the stud bay is open. In the drywall, centred on y 0 and 190 up, a 1-gang cut-out made from the box's template: 2-1/4 x 3-5/8 in (57.2 wide, 92.1 tall). 2) Box: a blue PVC 1-gang old-work box with mounting ears and two swing clamps (for example a Carlon B114R: 4-1/8 L x 2-1/4 W x 2-3/4 D in, 14 cu in, 56.7 g). Its front rim and ears (2.5 mm thick, 57 x 104.8 mm) bear on the wall 6.4 mm above and below the cut-out; the body behind them is 54 x 89 mm at the ears and 50 x 85 mm at the back (moulding draft), with 2.5 mm walls. Two clamp screws (7.4 mm pan heads, #2 Phillips) on its centre line 37 mm above and below its middle, heads on the ears' face. Each drives a white plastic clamp arm (19 mm from the screw's axis, 7 wide, 3 thick), delivered folded inside the box 24 mm behind the ears: turned clockwise, the screw swings it out through a slot in the box's end wall to its stop, then draws it toward the ears onto the back of the drywall (in the simulation about 3.4 turns from folded to clamped; see fidelity). 3) Cable: 14/2 NM-B with ground, white, 9.4 mm wide (maker's 0.372 in) and about 4.5 mm thick, 91 g/m. It comes down inside the stud bay through a 3/4 in hole drilled in the top plate (stapled on top of the plate), 73 mm behind the wall's face and 17 mm to the robot's right of the cut-out's centre line; from the plate's underside it hangs 112 mm straight down, bends forward through a quarter turn of about 37 mm radius, runs out through the cut-out 30 mm above its centre, and goes in through a port (12 x 7 mm, with a clamp tab) in the top of the box's back wall. Inside it runs under the box's top wall and out of the front, where its last 80 mm is bent up, 12 mm radius, to stand in front of the top ear to the right of the top screw, within 25 mm of the wall. 152 mm (6 in) of cable is past the back wall. Start: the box hangs on the cable, square to the wall and level with the cut-out, its ears' back faces 78 mm in front of the wall (its back 11 mm short of it), nothing else holding it. 4) Screwdriver: a #2 Phillips stubby, 92 mm overall (6 mm shaft 42 mm long, red and yellow octagonal handle 30 mm across flats, 50 mm long), 50 g, standing tip down in its block with the cross of its tip along x and y. 5) Block: beech, 50 x 50 x 44 mm tall, with a 10 mm square hole through it, fixed to the table centred at x 170, y -170; the screwdriver's shaft is in the hole and its handle rests on the block. Both arms start at their ready poses, grippers open. Nothing else is on the table; the layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every control step; the score is the last step's. Flush: the box's centre within 2 mm of the cut-out's centre, and each ear's back face within 0.5 mm of the wall at both its corners. A clamp is tight when its arm has swung out 80 degrees or more (90 at its stop) and presses the back of the drywall with 20 N or more, and its screw has turned no more than 0.25 turn without the screwdriver in it (in it: the tip in the recess's cross, within 2.5 mm of the screw's axis, the shaft within 25 degrees of the axis). Put down: the screwdriver's lowest point within 5 cm of the table top (on the table or in its block), not in a screw. Hands off: every point of both grippers 3 cm or more from the box and from the screwdriver. Still: the box and the screwdriver each moved 1 mm or less over the last 1 s. 1.0: flush, both clamps tight, screwdriver put down, hands off and still, all held for 1 s (20 steps), which ends the trial. 0.75: flush and both clamps tight. 0.5: flush and one clamp tight. 0.25: the box was flush at some point. Else 0. Cable: the three higher scores also need the cable still fed into the box, no more than 15 mm of it drawn back out through the port (a ruler on the tail: its end stands 51 mm above the top ear's upper edge at the start). Real trial: the wall section's back is open, so after the trial each arm is checked from behind (swung out over the board, a 0.1 mm feeler will not pass under it); tight also means a further quarter turn with the screwdriver takes force, and the box moves 0.5 mm or less (feeler gauge) when pulled straight out with 20 N on a luggage scale hooked over its rim; ear gaps with a 0.5 mm feeler gauge; that each screw was turned only with the screwdriver, from the video.
reset_notes: Back both clamp screws out (counter-clockwise) until each arm has swung back into the box; pull the box out of the wall, drawing the cable out after it. Push the cable through the port until 152 mm is past the back wall (the tail's end 51 mm above the top ear's upper edge), rebend it by hand to the start shape (a cardboard template of the bends helps) and hang the box 78 mm in front of the wall, level with the cut-out. Replace the cable when its jacket creases, and the drywall when the cut-out's edges or the board behind the clamps show crushing. Stand the screwdriver in its block. For a real box, first run each clamp up its screw, arm held folded, until 3.5 turns are left (see README).
fidelity: CPU PhysX, rigid bodies. Clamps: a screw, a threaded hub (mimic joint) and an arm on a 40 N/mm spring; thread 4 mm/turn (real ~0.8): 3.4 turns, not ~15. Cable: hinged links in the box's articulation; each bend is an 8 N m/rad spring capped at 0.12 N m whose set angle follows once it gives, and the entry's clamp likewise at 8 N (a material law in code); it bends in one plane and cannot leave the box. Gypsum is rigid. Cable stiffness and forces, frictions, the 20 N: estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (6,000 steps; both arms folded down, the left gripper came up beside the hanging box once; the box was never pushed in and the screwdriver not touched); scripted demo: 1.0 (success at step 3,589)
